title: Kerala Egg Curry

method: Begin by boiling the eggs for 10 minutes, then immediately transfer them to cold water to stop the cooking process.

Heat coconut oil in a saucepan, then add mustard seeds. Once they start to splutter, introduce cardamom, fennel seeds, ginger, garlic, chili, onions, and curry leaves, along with a pinch of salt. Cook for 3-4 minutes.

Kerala Egg Curry 
dinner for two | 30 minute recipe | date night | meal prep friendly | easy recipe

Nutrition: 
Macros: C: 18 | F: 26 | P: 16
Calories:  344 per serve 
Makes 3 serving

Ingredients
6 eggs 
1 tbsp coconut oil 
1 tsp mustard seeds
3 green cardamoms
1 tsp fennel seeds
2 onions, thinly sliced
1 tbsp minced ginger garlic paste
2 green chillies finely chopped, adjust as per taste 
2 sprigs curry leaves
1 tbsp red chilli powder
1 tsp turmeric powder
1 tbsp coriander powder
2 tomatoes, sliced 
200 ml coconut milk 
1/2 cup water 
for garnish, handful of coriander 

Method 

begin by boiling the eggs for 10 minutes, then immediately transfer them to cold water to stop the cooking process. 
heat coconut oil in a saucepan, then add mustard seeds. Once they start to splutter, introduce cardamom, fennel seeds, ginger, garlic, chili, onions, and curry leaves, along with a pinch of salt. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
add in the RCP + haldi + coriander 
add the tomatoes and cook for a few minutes till the tomatoes go mushy ( while its cooking down, peel the eggs ) 
add in the coconut milk, some water and stir then add the boiled eggs
let it simmer for a few minutes and enjoy :) 

chefs tips:
for higher protein lower fat in this recipe, use more egg whites less yolks :) personally i eat one normal egg + 2 egg whites per serve 
i enjoy my curries thinner so i can dip the paratha in it but if you want a thicker curry, use less water and only one tomato
